item.html:
Detailed Commercial Roof Condition Reports

A commercial roof is one of the largest capital liabilities on any property. Whether you are acquiring a new commercial facility, renewing a triple-net lease, or simply planning your annual maintenance budget, you cannot afford to guess about the condition of your roof. Hidden moisture trapped in the insulation, failing membrane seams, or undocumented storm damage can lead to massive, unexpected expenses.

At Core Four Roofing, we take the guesswork out of commercial asset management. Our expert technicians perform exhaustive, top-to-bottom roof assessments. We evaluate the structural integrity of the roof deck, test the condition of the insulation, inspect all complex drainage systems, and scrutinize every inch of flashing around HVAC units and parapet walls. The result is a highly detailed Real Estate Roof Condition Report that gives you the exact facts, photos, and financial estimates you need to make confident, informed decisions.

item.html: Frequently Asked Questions About Commercial Inspections
item.text: Frequently Asked Questions About Commercial Inspections

items.q: What exactly is included in a Real Estate Roof Condition Report?
items.a: Our comprehensive reports include a detailed analysis of the roof's current age, remaining expected lifespan, the condition of the membrane and flashing, core sample results (to check for wet insulation), high-resolution photos of any vulnerabilities, and accurate cost estimates for immediate repairs or future replacement.

items.q: How often should a commercial property be inspected?
items.a: Industry standards dictate that commercial flat roofs should be formally inspected at least twice a year—ideally in the spring and fall—as well as immediately following any severe weather events, such as high winds, heavy hail, or nearby tornadoes.

items.q: Do you take core samples during an inspection?
items.a: Yes, with the property owner's authorization. A core sample is a small, easily repairable cut made into the roof to determine the exact composition of the roofing layers and to check if the underlying insulation is saturated with water, which is critical data for determining if a roof can be repaired or must be fully replaced.

items.q: Can this inspection help with my commercial insurance policy?
items.a: Absolutely. Providing a clean, professional bill of health for your roof can sometimes assist in negotiating insurance premiums or preventing coverage drops. Conversely, if we find storm damage, our report serves as the foundation for filing a successful claim.
